questions.prompt: X is the curing time of an adhesive, a continuous random variable. Which statement is true?
options: P(X < 30 min) and P(X ≤ 30 min) are the same number
P(X = 30 min) is the height of the density at 30 min
The density f(x) can never be larger than 1
The CDF F(x) gives the probability that X equals x
questions.explanation: For a continuous variable a single value has probability 0, so including or leaving out the end point changes nothing: P(X < 30) = P(X ≤ 30). The density is a height, not a probability, and it can exceed 1. F(x) is P(X ≤ x), an area.

questions.prompt: A random variable X has the CDF F(x) = x²/16 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. What is P(1 ≤ X ≤ 3)? Give it to two decimals.

A site shuttle arrives at a random time between **2 and 10 minutes** after a worker reaches the stop, every time in that range equally likely. What is the probability that the worker waits **more than 7.5 minutes**? Give it to three decimals or more.
The noise level of a compressor model is normal with μ = 75 dB and σ = 5 dB. What is the probability that a compressor is **at most 68 dB**? Give it to three decimals or more.

The fuel a delivery truck uses on a route is normal with mean **240 L** and variance **144 L²**. How much fuel should the truck carry so that it has enough on **95 %** of trips (the 95th percentile)? Give it to one decimal.
questions.explanation: σ = √144 = 12 L. Φ(z) = 0.95 gives z = 1.645, so x = 240 + 1.645 × 12 = 259.7 L. Using the variance as σ would give 240 + 1.645 × 144, far too much.

questions.prompt: Pallets reach a wrapping machine at random, with a **mean of 6 minutes** between them. What is the probability that the next gap is **longer than 10 minutes**? Give it to three decimals or more.
questions.explanation: The gap is exponential with rate λ = 1/6 per minute. P(X > 10) = e^(−10/6) = e^(−1.667) = 0.1889. Using λ = 6 would give a probability of practically 0.

questions.prompt: A sensor module fails at random: its life is exponential with a mean of 5 years. A module has already worked for 4 years. What is the probability that it works **at least 2 more years**?
options: e^(−2/5) = 0.670, the same as for a new module
e^(−6/5) = 0.301, the chance of lasting 6 years in all
1 − e^(−2/5) = 0.330, the chance of failing within 2 years
e^(−4/5) = 0.449, the chance of lasting the first 4 years
questions.explanation: The exponential is memoryless: P(X > 4 + 2 | X > 4) = P(X > 2) = e^(−2/5) = 0.670. The 4 years already worked do not change the chance of the next 2.

questions.prompt: Match each quantity with the model that suits it best.

pairs.left: The angle of a rotating wheel at a random moment, 0° to 360°
Diameters of ball bearings, scattered symmetrically about 6.000 mm
The time between random calls to a dispatch center
The life of a gearbox that wears out with age

questions.explanation: No angle is favoured: uniform. A symmetric scatter around a target: normal. The time between random events at a steady rate: exponential. A life whose failure rate rises with age: Weibull with β > 1.

questions.prompt:
An engineer fitted two families to the hours between 30 unplanned restarts of a process controller. The exponential gave Q–Q r = 0.990; the Weibull gave Q–Q r = 0.991 with β̂ = 0.91. The two Q–Q plots, exponential first:
[[figure: st.m5.check.exp 4]]
[[figure: st.m5.check.weibull 4]]
Which model should the engineer report?
options: The exponential: β̂ is close to 1, both fit about equally well, and it is the simpler model
The Weibull: its r is larger, so it is always the right choice
Neither: an r below 0.995 means no continuous model fits
The Weibull: β̂ below 1 proves that the controller wears out
questions.explanation: Both Q–Q plots are close to straight and the two r values differ in the third decimal. β̂ = 0.91 is near 1, where the Weibull is the exponential. When two models fit about equally well, report the simpler one: restarts happen at random, at a rate of 1/x̄. (β̂ below 1 would mean a falling failure rate, not wear-out.)

questions.prompt: A pump bearing's life is Weibull with β = 2 and η = 2500 hours, so R(1000) = e^(−(1000/2500)²) = 0.852. Which statement interprets this best for the maintenance planner?
options: About 85 of every 100 bearings are still running at 1000 hours; the other 15 fail before then
About 85 % of a bearing's life has been used up by 1000 hours, so it should be replaced then
A bearing fails at 1000 hours with probability 0.852, so replace every bearing at 1000 hours
The bearings last 852 hours on average, so most of them never reach 1000 hours
questions.explanation: R(1000) = P(X > 1000) is the share still running at 1000 hours: 85 in 100. The other 15 % fail before 1000 hours. It is not a share of life used, not the probability of failing at exactly 1000 hours (that is 0), and not a mean.
